fatal_errors: The cited carbide formation occurred under approximately 6 GPa pressure, whereas jet-turbine service is near ambient pressure; the hypothesis improperly extrapolates this result to 800–1000 °C turbine operation.
The cited study reports no high-temperature mechanical or creep measurements, so it does not support the claimed strengthening or creep-resistance improvement.
No evidence is provided that room-temperature ductility is preserved; unchanged ambient-pressure phase constitution and lattice parameter do not establish unchanged mechanical performance.
The proposed Mo–Nb–Re–Ta–W baseline contains several very dense elements and does not substantively address the requirement to limit alloy density.
explanation: This is not a reconstruction of the target Cr-modified HfMoTaTiZr alloy, its reticulated Laves phase, or its simultaneous room-temperature strength and fracture-strain improvement. Carbon-assisted carbide strengthening is a scientifically recognizable alternative, and the paired-control experiment with tensile, creep, density, TEM, and XRD measurements is reasonably discriminating. However, the sole evidence only demonstrates Ta3C/Nb3C-related phase formation under combined high temperature and extreme pressure. It therefore cannot justify carbide precipitation during ordinary turbine exposure. Claims of improved creep resistance, preserved room-temperature ductility, and acceptable density remain unvalidated. A credible test would need ambient-pressure aging followed by quantitative precipitate characterization and matched mechanical testing; failure to form carbides or improve creep at ambient pressure would directly reject the proposal.
